why: rehearse() raises ReaderFailed out of read_tree() before it builds the record, so a run that exhausts a read's schema retries leaves nothing on disk: the reads that DID pass, every attempt's cost_usd and session_id, and the failure itself are lost. A record of truth may not drop an error (Law 7), and the spend is real money nobody can see.

occurrences.contrast: every completed run records meta.cost_usd (measured on 5 control records: 0.388382, 0.727141, 0.506664, 0.567637, 0.958228)
occurrences.exact_refusal: ReaderFailed: read 3: no tree passed the schema in 3 attempts — last lacks: nodes[14].step: 'D14' names a decision the ticket does not carry ...
occurrences.measured: 2026-10-08, F22(b) control rerun for ticket 80518446bfc8: 41202d4c8d3b with D14 removed, scratch commons control_commons_1791444040 — reads 1 and 2 completed, read 3 failed 3 attempts; the scratch rehearsals/ dir holds no record, and the only trace is the traceback in the caller's stdout
occurrences.the_fix_when_taken: not designed here; the candidate is a failed record written through the same door (clean: null, the completed reads, every attempt's meta, the ReaderFailed text) before the raise propagates
